title: How tall would your neck be if you had a crane's ratio?
description: A crane of height one hundred fifty five centimetres has its neck and the rest of its body in the ratio four to six. The terms are added to get ten groups, the neck is four of them, and the same fraction is applied to a person's height.
teaching_notes: One idea: the first term over the sum of the terms is the fraction of the whole. Watch for students who write the neck as four sixths of the rest of the body instead of four tenths of the whole height.

video_script.why: The child uses the sharing method to turn a ratio of two parts into a fraction of the whole and applies it to another height.
video_script.substitution: Add the terms to get the groups, write the neck as its groups over all the groups, then take that fraction of the height.
video_script.anchor: a crane standing beside a height bar of one hundred fifty five centimetres, with its neck and the rest of its body marked
video_script.payoff_line: your neck would be four tenths of your height
maths_rules: groups = 4 + 6 = 10; the neck is 4 of the 10 groups, so 4/10 of the height
example height 150 cm: 150 / 10 = 15; 15 x 4 = 60 cm of neck
video_script.design: One idea: the neck is its groups out of all the groups, a fraction of the whole height. The crane and its height bar stay in the anchor band and the working goes on the board.
open_questions: The worklist uses a height of 150 cm as the example for a person, which is not in the book.

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This question is from your book.
<bookmark mark='crane'/>A crane is one hundred fifty five centimetres tall.
<bookmark mark='ratio'/>Its neck and the rest of its body are in the ratio four to six.
<bookmark mark='person'/>Suppose your neck and the rest of your body had this ratio too.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>How tall would your neck be?

beats.on_screen: the crane and the person hold still and the question mark glows

marks.stop: the question mark glows in the accent colour

narration: <bookmark mark='stop'/>Think and tell.

marks.groups: the counters split into 4 groups of 3
marks.parts: the parts 9 and 3 appear under the groups
marks.same: the crane slides beside the counters

narration: <bookmark mark='example'/>The example in your book shared twelve counters in the ratio three to one.
<bookmark mark='groups'/>Three plus one is four, so there are four equal groups of three.
<bookmark mark='parts'/>One part takes three groups and the other takes one, which makes nine and three.
<bookmark mark='same'/>We will use the groups the same way as the example in your book.

beats.on_screen: Given: crane height 155 cm, neck : rest = 4 : 6

marks.given: the crane height and the ratio are written

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, a crane one hundred fifty five centimetres tall.
Its neck and the rest of its body are in the ratio four to six.

beats.on_screen: To find: the neck for your height

marks.find: the thing to find is written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find how long your neck would be.

beats.on_screen: groups = 4 + 6 = 10; the neck is 4 of the 10 groups, so 4/10 of the height

marks.neck: the neck is 4 of the 10 groups, so 4/10 of the height, is written

narration: <bookmark mark='groups'/>Step one, add the terms four and six to get ten groups.
<bookmark mark='neck'/>The neck takes four of the ten groups, so it is four tenths of the whole height.
<bookmark mark='one'/>Step two, try it on the crane. Divide one hundred fifty five by ten, which gives fifteen point five.
<bookmark mark='four'/>Four groups make sixty two centimetres, so the crane's neck is sixty two centimetres.

beats.on_screen: say your height is 150 cm: 150 ÷ 10 = 15; 15 × 4 = 60 cm

marks.say: say your height is 150 cm is written

narration: <bookmark mark='say'/>Step three, say your height is one hundred fifty centimetres.
<bookmark mark='one'/>Divide by ten to get fifteen.
<bookmark mark='four'/>Four groups make sixty centimetres, so your neck would be sixty centimetres.

beats.on_screen: put the answer back: rest = 150 − 60 = 90; 60 + 90 = 150; 60 : 90 = 4 : 6 (divide both by 15)

marks.back: the words put the answer back in the question are written

narration: <bookmark mark='back'/>Step four, put the answer back in the question.
<bookmark mark='rest'/>The rest of the body is one hundred fifty minus sixty, which is ninety.
<bookmark mark='sum'/>Sixty plus ninety is one hundred fifty, the whole height.
<bookmark mark='ratio'/>Divide both by fifteen and we get four to six.

beats.on_screen: Answer: 4/10 of your height (60 cm for a height of 150 cm)
narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>Your neck would be four tenths of your height.
